# rEFInd GUI release updates

Renovate's dedicated regex manager captures `REFIND_GUI_VERSION` as
`currentValue` and the adjacent `REFIND_GUI_SHA256` as `currentDigest`.
The `github-release-attachments` datasource identifies the current RPM from
its checksum sidecar and maps its versioned filename to the next release.
The generic manager accepts only `github-releases`, preventing a duplicate
rEFInd dependency. Keep the two assignments adjacent.

GitHub's generated tag archive is not an uploaded release attachment.
`refind-checksums.yml` handles its separate pin:

1. On an opened, synchronized, or reopened PR targeting `main`, check that
   the author is `renovate[bot]`, the branch belongs to this repository, and
   its name matches `renovate/jlobue10-refind_gui-[0-9]+.x` exactly.
2. Run only the base commit's updater. Read the head's build script through
   the API as data; never check out or execute PR code with the write token.
3. Download the versioned upstream RPM and verify it against Renovate's pin.
   Download and hash the matching source archive from the fixed upstream URL.
   Reject malformed/duplicate assignments and unexpected RPM bytes.
4. Commit only the source hash replacement, with the observed PR head as
   parent. Update the branch without force; a concurrent push fails safely.
5. Explicitly dispatch `build.yml` on that branch with `verified_head` set
   to the verified commit. No-op runs dispatch too, so rerunning a failed
   dispatch does not require another commit. Stale events do nothing.

The image still checks **both committed SHA-256 pins** before installation
or extraction. It never fetches a checksum to trust at image-build time.
Missing or renamed RPM assets (including a Fedora suffix change) require a
reviewed packaging change; the updater refuses to silently substitute one.

The updater has only `contents: write`, `pull-requests: read`, and
`actions: write`. No PAT or extra repository secret is needed. Explicit
dispatch avoids relying on PR events generated by `GITHUB_TOKEN` writes.
The original Renovate PR event skips the image job until the updater has
finished. The dispatched build checks out the verified SHA. Registry
publication/signing is disabled when `verified_head` is supplied, as well
as on non-default branches. Other PR builds retain their existing behavior.

## Activation and recovery

The updater must first land on `main`: `pull_request_target` deliberately
uses trusted base code. Merely adding it to an existing PR does not activate
it. For the introducing PR, verify both downloads locally and manually
dispatch the existing `build.yml` workflow on the PR branch, supplying its
commit SHA as `verified_head`. Do not run PR code in a privileged target job
as a bootstrap shortcut.

For subsequent failures, rerun the checksum workflow from Actions. If the
head moved, use the run for the latest synchronize event. If needed, reopen
the PR to generate a fresh event. Repository/organization policy must allow
the declared token permissions and Actions dispatches; failures are reported
in the checksum job, not bypassed.

## Validation

Run the stdlib-only updater tests:

```sh
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

Install `renovate@44.155.8` in a disposable development directory with its
supported Node 24 runtime and RE2 dependency. Set `RENOVATE_ROOT` to that
installation's `node_modules/renovate` directory, then from this repository:

```sh
node "$RENOVATE_ROOT/dist/config-validator.js" --strict .github/renovate.json5
node tests/refind-renovate.mjs
```

The second test uses Renovate's real extraction, attachment mapping, and
replacement implementations with historical v3.4.6/v3.4.7 sidecar fixtures.
It checks that only one rEFInd dependency is extracted, other annotated
dependencies remain, and only the version and RPM digest are replaced.
The Python tests cover future versions, no-op dispatch, denied branches and
forks, malformed input, RPM mismatch, and concurrent head changes.

References: [Renovate attachment implementation](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/blob/main/lib/modules/datasource/github-release-attachments/index.ts),
[trusted target workflows](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/securely-using-pull_request_target),
and [workflow triggering](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-when-workflows-run/trigger-a-workflow).
